lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

Success depends on our ability to continuously develop innovative technologies and market them effectively.
Top Kontrol is manufactured by US-based contract manufacturers, with the final assembly taking place at our Minnesota headquarters.
Our ability to grow depends on whether the market accepts our current and future products and services, and we cannot assure you that any of our offerings will achieve or maintain commercial success.
Our future success partially relies on our proprietary technology, technical know-how, and other intellectual property.
Our business's success heavily relies on the abilities and experience of our principal executive officer, J. Scott Sitra.
Sitra’s continued services, our future success will also depend on our ability to attract and retain additional key personnel.
We depend on third-party contract manufacturers who may not have adequate capacity to fulfill our needs or meet our quality and delivery objectives and timetables.

Under Nasdaq rules applicable to controlled companies, we are permitted to rely on certain exemptions from Nasdaq’s corporate-governance requirements, including exemptions from the requirements that a majority of our board of directors be independent and that our compensation and nominating and corporate-governance committees be composed entirely of independent directors.
Although we do not currently intend to rely on these exemptions, we could elect to do so in the future.
If we rely on one or more of these exemptions, you may not have the same protections afforded to stockholders of companies that are subject to all of Nasdaq’s corporate-governance requirements.
Even if we do not rely on the controlled-company exemptions, our dual-class structure and the concentration of voting power with Messrs.
As we do not expect to pay dividends in the foreseeable future, you must rely on price appreciation of our common stock for return on your investment.

Any determination to pay dividends in the future will be at the discretion of our board of directors and will depend on a variety of factors, including our financial condition, results of operations, cash-flow needs, capital-expenditure plans, contractual restrictions, debt-covenant requirements, regulatory considerations, tax consequences and other factors that our board may deem relevant.
As a result, you must rely on price appreciation of our common stock for any return on your investment.

Any payment of cash dividends in the future will be at the discretion of our Board of Directors and will depend upon our results of operations, earnings, capital requirements, contractual restrictions, and other factors deemed relevant by our directors.
We anticipate continuing to rely on equity sales of our common stock to fund our operations until we generate sufficient revenues to cover our operating expenses, which may never happen.
We may also rely on loans from management or significant shareholders, but there are no assurances that they will provide additional funds in the future.
Future realization of the deferred tax benefit depends on the existence of sufficient taxable income within the carryforward period under the Federal tax laws.
